diagrams.title: From Log Sources to SIEM and Alerting
diagrams.subtitle: Follow the flow: sources emit, protocols transport, the SIEM correlates, the analyst tunes.

nodes.label: Systems & applications
nodes.detail: System logs, application events, performance counters, and errors. The richest source of local context.

nodes.label: Network infrastructure
nodes.detail: Interfaces, flows, sessions, and alarms from network devices.
nodes.exam: Without network telemetry, east-west traffic remains invisible.

nodes.label: syslog
nodes.detail: Standard transport for event messages to the collector. Simple, widely adopted format.

nodes.label: NetFlow / SNMP
nodes.detail: NetFlow describes who talks to whom and on which port; SNMP reads counters and receives traps.
nodes.exam: SCAP, on the other hand, standardizes compliance — outside the books, §4.4.

nodes.label: Port mirroring
nodes.detail: Copies traffic to a sensor or packet analyzer for deep inspection without interrupting traffic.
nodes.exam: SPAN depends on the switch and can drop packets under saturation.

nodes.label: SIEM
nodes.detail: Normalizes, timestamps, stores, and correlates events. It is a platform, not a sensor.
nodes.exam: Aggregation precedes correlation: you can only correlate what has been collected.

nodes.label: Alerts
nodes.detail: Actionable notification: what to look at, why, and how urgent. A false negative remains an undetected incident.
nodes.exam: True positive = real incident detected; false negative = real incident missed.

nodes.label: Alert tuning
nodes.detail: Documented adjustment of thresholds and exclusions to reduce noise without losing sensitivity.
nodes.exam: Never disable an entire rule just to silence a legitimate source.

nodes.label: Dashboard / NMS
nodes.detail: Summary views of alert status and device health. These are outputs, not sources.
nodes.exam: A dashboard does not replace collection: it reflects it.

quiz.question: Which step normalizes and correlates events before alerts are generated?
